The Kalshi demo API in fifteen minutes

Everything below is drawn from Kalshi's own documentation and from live demo responses. Each claim carries a link. Where a detail could not be confirmed it is called out in the flagged list rather than smoothed over.

The one-paragraph version. Kalshi runs a regulated event-contract exchange. Its Trade API is a REST + WebSocket service with identical shapes in production and demo, differing only in host. Market-data reads are public; anything touching money needs RSA-PSS request signing over the exact path. Prices are fixed-point strings (0.4200), counts are fixed-point strings (13.00), and order books publish bids only — the opposite side is derived as 1 − price. The legacy order-placement endpoints now return 410 Gone; trading moved to a V2 endpoint with a single-book bid/ask vocabulary. The demo exchange uses mock funds and its prices can diverge from production, so it is a build target, not a price source.

2 · What needs a key and what does not

Public — no credentials

  • GET /markets, /markets/{ticker}, /markets/trades
  • GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook (batch order books too)
  • GET /events, /events/{ticker}, GET /series, /series/{ticker}
  • GET /series/{s}/markets/{t}/candlesticks
  • GET /exchange/status

Verified by calling them unauthenticated against the demo host.

Signed — RSA-PSS

  • GET /portfolio/balance, /portfolio/positions, /portfolio/fills, /portfolio/orders
  • POST /portfolio/events/orders (place), and its cancel/amend/decrease siblings
  • Every WebSocket connection, even for public channels

Headers: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, -TIMESTAMP (ms), -SIGNATURE = base64 RSA-PSS-SHA256 over timestamp + METHOD + path. docs ↗

3 · Data shapes you must get right

rulewhat it means in practicesource
Fixed-point stringsyes_bid_dollars: "0.4200", volume_fp: "13.00". Parse as decimal, never float; prices accept 2–4 dp on input, responses emit up to 6. fixed point ↗
Bids-only bookorderbook_fp.yes_dollars and .no_dollars are bid ladders ascending by price, best bid last. Best YES ask = 1 − best NO bid. order book ↗
Empty book ≠ errorAn unknown or empty ticker returns 200 with empty arrays, not 404. Code that treats empty as "market missing" will be wrong. order book ↗
Tick size is dataRead price_ranges: [{start,end,step}] per market; do not hard-code 1-cent ticks. The structure name is not the contract. fixed point ↗
Order directionbid ≡ yes, ask ≡ no, always; direction never changes the price. Legacy action/side are deprecated. order direction ↗
Lifecycleinitialized → active → closed → determined → finalized, plus inactive, disputed, amended. result is set at determined; money moves at finalized. lifecycle ↗
Orders after closeOnce close_time passes, every order operation — including cancels — is rejected with MARKET_INACTIVE. lifecycle ↗
Rate limitsToken buckets per bucket type; X-RateLimit-* headers on every response; 429 carries no Retry-After. Balance has its own bucket (1/s on Basic). rate limits ↗
Placing ordersLegacy /portfolio/orders writes return 410 Gone. Use POST /portfolio/events/orders; a 201 means accepted, not resting — check remaining_count. create order v2 ↗
Candlesticksperiod_interval ∈ {1, 60, 1440} minutes, at most 5 000 periods per request, start_ts/end_ts in seconds. Recent candles can lag a few seconds. candlesticks ↗
Settled ≠ in the live datasetMarkets settled before the historical cutoff only appear in /historical/*. Absence from /markets?status=settled is not proof of no settlement. lifecycle ↗

4 · Fees are part of every strategy result

The published schedule charges takers ceil_centicent(M × 0.07 × C × P × (1 − P)) and makers 0.0175 instead of 0.07. There is no settlement fee and no membership fee. The table's own worked example: 100 contracts at $0.50 costs $1.75. Any backtest that ignores this overstates a 10-cent move by roughly a third. Fee schedule (PDF) ↗

5 · What the demo environment is for — and what it is not

Good for

  • Building and testing every request shape, including signed ones, with mock money.
  • Exercising lifecycle handling: markets close, determine and finalize on the demo too.
  • Reproducing bugs without risking capital; demo API keys are separate from production.

Not good for

  • Real prices. Kalshi states demo prices may diverge from production, and in this capture most five-topic markets had zero volume and one-sided books.
  • Liquidity conclusions. The ladders here hold hundreds of contracts, not market depth.
  • Strategy proof. One instrument with 16 usable hourly bars cannot validate anything.

6 · How this repository uses it

Public reads only, from the viewer's browser, with a committed snapshot as fallback; no key, no orders, paper trading priced strictly off recorded quotes. That is a deliberate limit, and it is why every performance number on the strategies page says "simulated" in the same sentence.
